text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Essay - 01
A distinctive costume can be part of an evening with room
for different preferences.
Pexels · 29225548
A little room to choose
A welcoming Halloween event gives people choices rather than testing everyone’s courage. At our neighborhood gathering, we
wanted a lively atmosphere without pressuring guests to enjoy the same activities. Clear options and careful preparation proved more
useful than an increasingly elaborate spectacle.
First, we made two experiences easy to identify. A lantern-lit route led to the main attraction; a quieter room offered pumpkin carving
and warm drinks. Volunteers explained both at the entrance, allowing guests to change their minds without having to justify their
preferences.
Practical details mattered just as much. Only when we tested a costume outside did we notice that its mask restricted the wearer’s
view. We adjusted it and checked the route for obstacles. Ingredient labels and non-food treats also helped guests decide what suited
them.
The event worked because its atmosphere invited participation while its arrangements preserved a sense of control. Preparation did
not remove the surprise; it removed avoidable pressure. Next year, we would retain that balance: make the possibilities clear,
anticipate small obstacles, and leave people room to choose.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a position; develop two distinct points with concrete examples; draw them together in the conclusion.
Each body paragraph needs a distinct supporting point and a concrete example. The conclusion draws the argument together without
introducing a third proposal.
Outline four paragraphs improving a school fair. Include two different changes, a concrete example for each, and a conclusion linking
their benefits.
